must_fix: Bind the abstract/results 12/12 seed-averaged ΔECE claim (and Wilcoxon p=2.4e-04) to uncalibrated (`none`) cells. results/stats_tests.json only records that sign count for calibrator=none (wilcoxon_delta_ece_gt0_s1.5_none_dataset_model_means). The abstract currently places “all 12/12 dataset×model means are positive” immediately after the temperature/isotonic/histogram clause, which is not what the seed-averaged test licenses.

Name closest prior work in running text, not only by cite key. Related work says “unsupervised recalibration … \cite{pampari2020unsupervised}” and “domain-drift … \cite{tomani2021posthoc}” then “those papers already predict.” Write Pampari & Ermon and Tomani et al. once so the attribution cannot be misread; lit_review.md already has the correct pair (Pampari & Ermon), matching verified.bib (Anusri Pampari, S. Ermon; arXiv 2006.16405).
weaknesses: This is a confirmation study. Ovadia et al., Tomani et al., and Pampari & Ermon already predict that confidence/calibration degrades under shift and that i.i.d. post-hoc maps are not a complete fix; Tibshirani et al. already predict that unweighted split conformal loses coverage when exchangeability breaks. Related work admits this. The residual contribution is the same qualitative story on sklearn LogReg/RF/HistGradientBoosting under a synthetic frozen-label Gaussian mean-shift versus pairing-preserving selection—not a new phenomenon and not a new calibrator.

Novelty is scoped to a 47-entry self-built, API-verified bibliography that the authors themselves describe as “mostly deep-net calibration and conformal theory, not a systematic search of applied tabular-drift venues.” That caveat belongs in the paper (and is there), but “we did not find this exact measurement” is still a tautological grid-gap: no one else ran this exact sklearn × four calibrators × perturbation-vs-selection spreadsheet. That is not evidence that tabular calibration-under-shift is unstudied.

Headline shift is input corruption (frozen y), not covariate shift. That is disclosed, and selection controls are weaker (quantile-slice cell-mean ΔECE 0.016 vs perturbation 0.113). The interesting scientific update is therefore negative: the originally advertised H1 (i.i.d. maps fail under covariate shift) is not supported. What remains is that breaking P(Y|X) by moving X and keeping y raises ECE—an outcome one would expect from any model that uses those coordinates, and one entangled with large accuracy drops (synthetic logreg 0.932→0.620 at s=1.5).

Evidence base is sklearn toys with no natural drift: breast_cancer, wine (~45-point test splits, 15 ECE bins), and two make_classification sets. Limitations say this (no OpenML/Folktables/WILDS). A confirmation on this corpus cannot license claims about “classical tabular models” in deployment.

lit_review.md is stale relative to the paper: the gap table and H1 still ask for “controlled covariate (not label) shift on tabular P(X)” and “i.i.d.-fitted post-hoc calibrators do not preserve ECE under covariate shift,” which analysis.md and the paper explicitly withdraw. If that file is part of the research record, it still sells a gap the experiments killed.

Abstract “remains positive after i.i.d. temperature, isotonic, or histogram maps” is licensed in the pooled-mean sense (temp 56/60, iso 53/60, hist 57/60) but omits the small-effect HGB×breast_cancer exception that analysis.md lists as an allowed caveat. Fine in the body; slightly smooth in the abstract.

Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005 already documented tree overconfidence and isotonic fragility on small n_cal; H2 was heterogeneous and killed. Unweighted coverage falling when labels are frozen off the observed x is not a surprise given broken exchangeability. Surviving content is one directional ECE effect plus one theory-predicted coverage plot plus a useful negative control.

Bibliographic hygiene (not fabrication): several verified.bib years follow arXiv upload rather than venue (tomani2021posthoc year=2020 vs CVPR 2021; key/year mismatches on uncited entries). Author names are S2-abbreviated (S. Ermon, R. Tibshirani). paper/candidates.json lists a different Tomani author set and arXiv id (2012.10923; Hussein/Mahapatra/Fischer) than verified.bib (2012.10988; Erdem/Cremers/Buettner). The paper cites the latter, which matches the CVPR 2021 record; candidates.json should not be treated as authoritative.
strengths: Honest genre label, repeated: abstract “This is an analysis result, not a new calibrator”; intro “We do not introduce a new calibrator”; limitations “Novelty is relative to paper/verified.bib (47 API-verified papers).” Title is mechanism-scoped (Feature Perturbation vs. Selection Shift), not a new-method oversell.

Gap claim is scoped, not “no paper anywhere”: intro states the 47-paper API-verified set, notes it is not a systematic search of applied tabular-drift venues, and calls it “a scoped gap, not a proof of absence.”

Related work states that Ovadia/Tomani/Pampari already predict the qualitative headlines (ECE rises; i.i.d. maps are not a complete fix) and writes the counterfactual: a surprising result would have been that logreg/RF/HGB stay calibrated under a mean-shift of used covariates with labels frozen. That is the correct novelty-cynic test, and they fail it on purpose.

Closest prior work is the right papers: Tomani et al. (post-hoc calibration under domain drift; verified authors Christian Tomani, Sebastian Gruber, Muhammed Ebrar Erdem, Daniel Cremers, Florian Buettner; arXiv 2012.10988 / CVPR 2021) and Pampari & Ermon (Unsupervised Calibration under Covariate Shift, arXiv 2006.16405). lit_review.md names “Pampari & Ermon,” matching verified.bib. No Pampari coauthor mismatch in the current text.

Killed hypotheses are reported as results: H2 (isotonic vs temperature vs n_cal) heterogeneous; H3 1-D “oracle” density-ratio weights did not restore coverage (0.744 vs 0.747). Original covariate-shift H1 is withdrawn. Selection control “does not support a claim that i.i.d. post-hoc calibration fails under covariate shift in general.”

Dataset and mechanism weaknesses are disclosed: frozen-label perturbation ≠ covariate shift; synthetic shift entangled with accuracy drop; small n; temperature on clipped tree probabilities is not Guo logit temperature; wine ECE noisy; no natural drift.

Mechanical citation check: all 21 unique \cite keys in paper/main.tex exist in paper/verified.bib (28 citation occurrences; 47 bib keys). Spot-check of well-known entries (Guo 2017; Ovadia 2019; Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005; Tibshirani/Barber/Candès/Ramdas 2019; Zadrozny & Elkan 2002; Kull et al. Dirichlet 2019; Vovk/Gammerman/Shafer; Grinsztajn 2022) matches real papers. Abstract numerical claims (51/60, mean ΔECE 0.113±0.149, 12/12, quantile-slice 0.016, coverage 0.913→0.778→0.608) are ⊆ analysis.md / numbers.tex.

Maps-help-or-hurt is not ranked into a fake winner: wine RF isotonic helps (−0.123 ECE) because the forest was already badly calibrated i.i.d.; breast-cancer logreg isotonic hurts (+0.074). That is an analysis result, not a bake-off.
